output.myth: Long ago a pale tree came up out of the Unflown on the back of a south wind. It had no leaves, only the trunk, and the sea had worn it smooth as bone. Tavo the Gale saw it, laughed, and flung it north over the rim of the water, where it should have fallen. It did not fall. Orrun felt it knock along his back under the waves and said nothing, which is how you know Orrun is annoyed. Sil saw it turning in the moonlight and thought it was one of Aun's kites, and she followed it a long way before the spray took it. My mother said that tree is still up there, going round the Lamp Road with its broken top pointed at home. Mesal the knot-lamp keeps an eye on it. If you find a pale log on the beach, do not burn it. Something on it is still counting its way back.
output.verse:
Pale trunk from the south
Tavo threw it north, and it
still counts its way home.
